text:
alex: Heads-up: ACME asked for a hard pin so their org always routes to Dedicated pool A even if autoscaler spills to shared. They want this for compliance during heavy batch jobs.

mika: Do we currently support a per-org "pin" that outranks automatic routing? I thought we only had allowlist rules for direct paths.

jamie: Not a hard outrank. We have prefer-dedicated but it's advisory; autoscaler can spill if capacity is low.

alex: Right — ACME wants an override policy: if header X-Redwood-Org: acme and org flag pinned=true then route to dedicated and fail closed if dedicated saturated (rather than spill). They explicitly want a 503 if dedicated can't accept.

sarah: That makes sense for their SLA but scary for availability. We should make it an opt-in shape in Console + require an approval flow + audit log.

mika: Also security: org header is user-controlled. We shouldn't rely on an unsigned header. Options: require token-scoped claim, or signed routing header (HMAC) generated by our control plane.

jamie: Proposal: order of precedence: 1) admin pin on org (console) 2) token-scoped allowlist (account-level) 3) signed header (for 3rd-party proxies). If admin pin present, routing policy -> dedicated with fail-closed. Otherwise fall back to prefer-dedicated.

alex: Works. For rollout, I suggest feature-flag rollout to 2 customers first (ACME, Zenwell). Add a debug trace to show why route chosen.

ops-bot: deploy-plan: create DB flag per org, add routing middleware to enforce pin, add audit event on decision. Scheduled window: Tue 03:00-05:00 UTC.

mika: Example routing rule (draft):
```json
{
  "match": {
    "header": "x-redwood-org",
    "value": "acme"
  },
  "priority": 1000,
  "action": {
    "route": "dedicated-pool-A",
    "fail_mode": "closed",
    "audit": true
  }
}
```

sarah: We need to record metrics: pin_evaluations, pin_enforced_count, pin_fallback_count, pin_503_count. Add per-org logging to Console route timeline.

jamie: Agree. Also ensure that KMS keys used for signed header verification are rotated and mapped per-tenant where applicable.

alex: One more UX thing: Console should show a clear warning: "Fail-closed means requests will 503 if dedicated capacity exhausted." And an admin checkbox with two-step confirmation.

mika: Edge case: what about batch jobs that hammer tokens concurrently? If we fail-closed we'll get a lot of 503s and noise. Recommend we add a soft-grace policy: a burst allowance (token bucket) that lets X requests spill for Y minutes before enforcing hard 503. Make that configurable per org.

jamie: Implementation note: runtime needs to evaluate in this order cheaply: check admin pin in cache, verify signed header (if present) lazily, fallback to token claims. Keep the hot path minimal. Also propagate reason_code in response header X-Redwood-Route-Reason.

sarah: Security sign-off required. I'll loop in security for header HMAC scheme + console audit retention policy.

alex: Action items: 1) jamie + mika to draft implementation PR with config schema + telemetry hooks. 2) sarah to create approval checklist and security ticket. 3) ops-bot to schedule rollout window. I'll own customer comms.

mika: I'll prototype the middleware today and post a tiny log sample.

ops-bot: noted. created ticket RW-3112 and assigned to @jamie.

alex: Thanks — let's keep it conservative for first deploy. :thumbsup:
